boatman.text: You arrived with no luggage and eyes full of storm. Are you a trader, messenger, or fugitive?

options.text: A messenger looking for safe routes through the town.
options.reply: Then remember the ghat. When all roads close, water remains.

pestel_notes.text: The Hooghly river route is the least disruptive extraction path.

options.text: I serve a future India that needs a hidden relic.
options.reply: Future? Say such things near soldiers and you will vanish before sunset.

options.text: Only a trader. I need no questions.
options.reply: Traders usually carry goods. Still, the river does not argue.

scholar.text: Tell me, stranger, why is Bengal politically sensitive this year?

options.text: The partition may weaken political unity and divide communities.
options.reply: You understand the wound without shouting. I will recommend you quietly.

pestel_notes.text: The 1905 Partition of Bengal risks weakening political unity and dividing communities.
Trust in Bengal depends on restraint, local knowledge, and avoiding future revelations.

options.text: The British are fools and must be destroyed.
options.reply: Anger is easy to plant and hard to uproot. Lower your voice.

options.text: I know the future and Bengal will suffer greatly.
options.reply: If this is madness, it is dangerous. If truth, more dangerous.

options.text: I am only a trader.
options.reply: Then you are an unconvincing one.

printer.text: The palace reads symbols before it reads words. What should I print for you?

options.text: A respectful invitation citing Professor Sen's recommendation.
options.reply: A clean line of ink opens more doors than a loud fist.

pestel_notes.text: The printing press can spread or contain information depending on wording.
Bazaar networks carry palace news faster than formal messengers.

options.text: A forged imperial order from London.
options.reply: That would draw Captain Haines like a match in darkness.

options.text: A prophecy naming me Kaal Rishi.
options.reply: Tempting theatre. Dangerous theatre.

minister.text: Why should the Nawab receive a stranger during such tense days?

options.text: I carry a scholar's recommendation and seek only a private historical audience.
options.reply: Measured words. I can arrange a guarded audience.

pestel_notes.text: Palace access is governed by reputation, protocol, and written invitation.

options.text: Because his treasury contains an object too dangerous for this era.
options.reply: You speak like a thief wearing a priest's shawl.

options.text: Deny me and history itself may punish you.
options.reply: Threats do not age well in palaces.

nawab.text: The Shakti Crystal is no trinket. Why should I surrender it?

options.text: I ask first and fail first. Your caution proves you are its rightful guardian.
options.reply: You accept refusal with discipline. Leave before soldiers notice you.

options.text: A sage says I must become Kaal Rishi, not a thief.
options.reply: The old name returns. If your restraint is true, the crystal may travel with you.

options.text: I will take it whether you bless the act or not.
options.reply: Then you will meet the prison under my court.

options.text: In the future, this crystal powers KAALCHAKRA.
options.reply: You reveal too much for a man asking history to stay calm.

sage.text: You failed because you asked as an agent. Ask again as a custodian. How will you build trust?

options.text: Protect local dignity, avoid prophecy, and let people choose.
options.reply: Good. A controlled reputation casts a small shadow.

pestel_notes.text: A controlled Kaal Rishi reputation works only when it protects local dignity.
The agent must avoid becoming a public symbol that changes the anti-partition movement.

options.text: Spread miracles so the Nawab fears me.
options.reply: Fear multiplies ripples.

options.text: Tell everyone I am from the future.
options.reply: Then you are not a traveler. You are a storm.
